request.idea: The lighthouse keeper of a small coastal town has vanished, and the lighthouse now shines with a cold green light that lures ships onto the rocks.

seeds.text: The wind carries the smell of cinnamon from where nobody bakes.
The beast is a transformed member of the town council.
Torches and lanterns gutter out after a short while.
To regain a title stolen from the family.
A shoe that always walks home.

concept.title: The Wrecker’s Lantern of Sortbro
concept.tagline: A green light lures ships to their doom, and every night a missing man’s shoe walks home.
concept.teaser: Above the cliffs of Ugletoft the lighthouse burns with a cold green light, and two ships have already broken their hulls on the rocks of Sortbro. Halfdan the lighthouse keeper has vanished, yet every morning one of his shoes stands on his sister’s doorstep, wet with seawater and smelling of cinnamon. Tonight the grain ship Three Sisters is due.
concept.premise: Halfdan the lighthouse keeper vanished three nights ago, and ever since, the lighthouse on Sortbro has burned with a cold green flame that lures ships onto the rocks. The town blames Thyra Bøgh, the strand reeve, and wants Halfdan hanged as the mad keeper. Behind it all stands Eske Sortfjer, councillor and spice merchant, who means to win back his family’s old title of strand reeve with his grandfather’s cursed Wrecker’s Lantern. The heroes must find Halfdan in the caves beneath Sortbro and put out the light before the grain ship Three Sisters is wrecked at midnight.
concept.truth: Sixty years ago the Sortfjer family lost the title of strand reeve of Ugletoft when Eske’s grandfather was caught lighting false lights on Sortbro; the council gave the title, and the right to every wreck on the coast, to the Bøgh family. Eske Sortfjer found his grandfather’s Wrecker’s Lantern in the family crypt: a brass lantern whose green flame drinks other light and makes the drowned rise as skeletons that obey whoever carries it. For a year Eske has smuggled untaxed cinnamon through the caves beneath Sortbro with the crew of the smuggler captain Ketil Vesterhavn, and a month ago Councillor Gorm Krogh, who had been asking questions about the customs, was pushed down into the Chapel of the Drowned, where the lantern’s curse turned him into a ghast. Three nights ago the smugglers seized Halfdan the keeper, who had seen their lights and refused Eske the key to the lamp room. When the Three Sisters is wrecked at midnight, Eske will have the smugglers carry Halfdan up to the lantern, ‘find’ him there in front of the council, put out the light as the town’s saviour and be elected strand reeve at dawn.
concept.conflict: Eske Sortfjer wants his family’s title and its right of wreck back, and he is willing to drown sailors and hang an innocent keeper for it, while the town has picked the wrong culprits.
concept.goal: Find Halfdan the keeper alive, put out the green light of the Wrecker’s Lantern before the grain ship Three Sisters reaches Sortbro at midnight, and prove to the council that Eske Sortfjer is behind it all.

objective.target: Halfdan, the missing lighthouse keeper of Sortbro
objective.state: Chained to an iron ring in the rock by the Tide Well, hungry, bruised and feverish, but alive. The ghast that was once Councillor Gorm Krogh guards him at the lantern’s bidding, and at midnight the smugglers are to carry him up to the lamp room so that Eske Sortfjer can ‘find’ him there.
objective.resolution: By force: defeat the ghast at the Tide Well, then break the chain (AC 19, 10 HP) or pick its lock with a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check using thieves’ tools; on a failure 10 minutes pass, and the noise calls the skeletons from the Chapel of the Drowned. Without a fight: get the key to the chain from Ketil Vesterhavn in the Cinnamon Cellar with a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check if the heroes tell him that Eske has promised the council to come up to the lighthouse with the town guard at midnight, just when the smugglers are due on the stair with Halfdan, and promise to let the smugglers sail away, or buy it for 50 gp; and a cleric who calls the ghast by the name Gorm Krogh and holds up his chain of office can make it step aside for 1 minute with a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check. Halfdan is weak (4 HP) but can walk, and he knows the hidden stair behind the chapel altar that climbs to the lamp room. If the heroes have not freed him by midnight, the smugglers carry him up to the lamp room, and Eske ‘finds’ him there beside the Wrecker’s Lantern in front of the council’s men.

concept.stakes: If the heroes fail, the grain ship Three Sisters is wrecked on Sortbro at midnight, twenty sailors drown and rise as Eske’s skeletons, and at dawn the council strips Thyra Bøgh of her title, hangs Halfdan as the mad keeper and makes Eske Sortfjer strand reeve, with the right to everything the sea brings ashore.

clock.start: At dusk the green light is already burning in the lighthouse on Sortbro, and the wrecks of two ships lie on the rocks. The council has gathered at the Anchor Inn in Ugletoft and is quarrelling over who is to blame, and far out at sea the grain ship Three Sisters shows as a small lantern on her way to the harbour.

ticks.event: Fog drifts in from the sea and the green light grows stronger: lanterns and torches in Ugletoft and on the cliffs go out after a minute and must be lit again.
ticks.sign: The harbour lanterns die one by one while the green light shines through the fog; by the cliff path the heroes can still reach the lighthouse in half an hour.

ticks.when: When the heroes first enter the Sea Maw
ticks.event: The smugglers’ lookout rings a small bell, and Ketil Vesterhavn sends a man up the hidden stair to warn Eske Sortfjer in the lamp room.
ticks.sign: A bell chimes faintly inside the cave, and wet footsteps vanish into the dark; anyone who gives chase at once can catch the runner before he reaches the stair.

ticks.event: The drowned sailors from the two wrecks rise on Wreck Beach and walk into the caves to guard them, Eske Sortfjer takes his place in the lamp room with the Wrecker’s Lantern, and the tide begins to fill the Sea Maw; after 5 hours the way in from the beach is closed, and only the hidden stair or a climb up the outside of the lighthouse leads to the lamp room.
ticks.sign: Bones rattle in the surf, wet footprints climb the beach, and the waves crash into the cave so hard that the smugglers’ boat bucks against the rock.

ticks.event: The Three Sisters steers for the green light and is wrecked on Sortbro, unless the lighthouse’s true light has been burning for at least 10 minutes; the smugglers carry Halfdan up to the lamp room, and Eske puts out the light in front of the council’s men.
ticks.sign: The ship’s bell clangs in panic out in the fog, and hull and masts groan as she strikes the rocks.

clock.costs: From Ugletoft to the lighthouse on Sortbro: half an hour by the cliff path; from the lighthouse down the path to Wreck Beach: a quarter of an hour. Searching a place thoroughly: 20 minutes. Walking through the caves from the Sea Maw to the Tide Well: half an hour without fights. A Short Rest: 1 hour. Near the green light, lanterns and torches go out after 1 minute; relighting one takes an action.
clock.deadline: After 6 hours, at midnight, the grain ship Three Sisters is wrecked on Sortbro, twenty sailors drown, and Halfdan is found beside the Wrecker’s Lantern as the culprit. The ship can only turn away if the green fire is out and the lighthouse’s true light is burning no later than 10 minutes before midnight.

concept.twist: The monster guarding Halfdan in the caves is Councillor Gorm Krogh, who discovered Eske’s smuggling and was pushed down into the Chapel of the Drowned; the lantern’s curse turned him into a ghast, but he still wears the rags of his councillor’s coat and carries a jar of pickled onions, and a last glimmer of the man can still be reached.
hooks: Vibeke, the keeper’s sister, finds the heroes at the Anchor Inn with a wet shoe in her hands: “It’s on my doorstep every morning. Halfdan isn’t dead, and he never lit that light.”

The cleric receives word from the temple in the next town: the drowned sailors from the two wrecks, laid to rest in the chapel beneath Sortbro, have vanished from their niches, and someone must give them peace.
The rogue gets a short message from an old contact, the smuggler captain Ketil Vesterhavn: “Don’t come to Ugletoft tonight. If you come anyway, come before midnight.”

villain.name: Eske Sortfjer
villain.nature: A respected spice merchant and councillor of Ugletoft, grandson of the last strand reeve of the Sortfjer line, who carries his grandfather’s cursed Wrecker’s Lantern.
villain.want: To take back the title of strand reeve that the council stripped from his family sixty years ago, and with it the right to every wreck on the coast. To Eske this is not theft but giving his family back its honour.
villain.plan: 1) Let the Wrecker’s Lantern burn in the lighthouse until ships founder and the town blames Thyra Bøgh, the strand reeve. 2) Keep Halfdan the keeper prisoner in the caves, guarded by the ghast. 3) After 4 hours, take his place in the lamp room with the lantern and let the drowned guard the caves. 4) At midnight, lure the grain ship Three Sisters onto Sortbro. 5) Have the smugglers carry Halfdan up to the lantern, ‘find’ him there, put out the light in front of the council’s men and be elected strand reeve at dawn.
villain.weakness: The Wrecker’s Lantern: if it is smashed (AC 13, 6 HP), or its flame is smothered with a cloth soaked in salt water from the Tide Well, the green light goes out and the drowned collapse. And Eske cannot bear to stand where his grandfather stood: faced with the council’s old judgment, Halfdan alive and a witness from the council, he would rather confess than flee like a common wrecker.

cast.name: Eske Sortfjer
cast.role: the villain, spice merchant and councillor of Ugletoft
cast.where: At the council meeting in the Anchor Inn in Ugletoft at dusk; after 4 hours in the lamp room at the top of the lighthouse on Sortbro, with the Wrecker’s Lantern.

cast.name: Halfdan
cast.role: the missing keeper of the Sortbro lighthouse
cast.where: Chained at the Tide Well in the caves beneath Sortbro, weak but alive.

cast.name: Vibeke
cast.role: the keeper’s sister, who finds his shoe on her doorstep every morning
cast.where: At the Anchor Inn at dusk, and afterwards in her house by the harbour in Ugletoft.

cast.name: Thyra Bøgh
cast.role: strand reeve of Ugletoft and eldest on the council, whom the town blames
cast.where: At the council meeting in the Anchor Inn in Ugletoft.

cast.name: Gorm Krogh
cast.role: the councillor who vanished a month ago, now a ghast in the caves
cast.where: At the Tide Well in the caves beneath Sortbro, where he guards Halfdan.

cast.name: Ketil Vesterhavn
cast.role: smuggler captain in Eske’s pay and an old contact of the rogue
cast.where: In the Cinnamon Cellar in the caves beneath Sortbro, with his crew.

factions.name: Ketil Vesterhavn’s smugglers
factions.want: Their pay in cinnamon and silver, and to get away before anyone hangs.
factions.method: Boats by night through the Sea Maw, knives and hooded lanterns.
factions.attitude: Hostile to strangers in the caves, but they fight for money, not for Eske: if they hear that Eske has promised the council to come up to the lighthouse with the town guard at midnight (his note to Ketil says nothing of it), they understand that they could be caught on the stair together with Halfdan, and they change sides or flee.

factions.name: The Council of Ugletoft
factions.want: Someone to blame before more ships are lost.
factions.method: A meeting at the Anchor Inn and a vote at dawn.
factions.attitude: Wary of strangers. Thyra Bøgh helps the heroes if they can clear her name; Eske’s friends on the council want Halfdan hanged.

factions.name: The Drowned
factions.want: To rest in peace in their niches.
factions.method: They rise in the light of the Wrecker’s Lantern and obey whoever carries it.
factions.attitude: Hostile, but a cleric who blesses them, or a light put out, gives them peace.

outline.title: The Shoe on the Doorstep
outline.purpose: Vibeke asks the heroes to find Halfdan; in the Anchor Inn the council quarrels over the green light, and the heroes meet Thyra Bøgh and Eske Sortfjer and get the first clues: the shoe, the smell of cinnamon, the old judgment against the Sortfjer family, and Councillor Gorm Krogh, who disappeared.

outline.title: The Keeper’s Room
outline.purpose: The heroes search the lighthouse on Sortbro: Halfdan’s logbook, the barred door to the tower and the smell of cinnamon from a crack in the rock; they work out that the way to the lamp room and to Halfdan runs through the caves.

outline.title: The Caves beneath Sortbro
outline.purpose: From Wreck Beach through the Sea Maw, the Cinnamon Cellar and the Chapel of the Drowned to the Tide Well: the smugglers, the drowned and the ghast that was Gorm Krogh; the heroes free Halfdan and find the hidden stair.

outline.title: The Wrecker’s Lantern
outline.purpose: At the top of the lighthouse Eske Sortfjer stands with the Wrecker’s Lantern while the Three Sisters steers for the rocks: the heroes must put out the green fire before midnight and expose Eske, so that Halfdan and Thyra Bøgh go free.

locationThemes.name: Wreck Beach
locationThemes.purpose: The beach below Sortbro with the wrecks of two ships, sand of crushed mussel shells and a line of single shoeprints leading into the Sea Maw; here the drowned rise after 4 hours.

locationThemes.name: The Sea Maw
locationThemes.purpose: The sea cave in the cliff where the smugglers’ boat lies behind an iron grate and a lookout keeps watch with a bell; lanterns go out after a minute, and the tide closes the cave after 5 hours.

locationThemes.name: The Cinnamon Cellar
locationThemes.purpose: The smugglers’ store of chests of cinnamon bark, branded with the black feather of the Sortfjer family; Ketil Vesterhavn and his crew, and Eske’s note.

locationThemes.name: The Chapel of the Drowned
locationThemes.purpose: An old cave chapel where the town priest laid out the dead from the two wrecks; the niches stand empty, the altar is desecrated, and behind it a hidden stair climbs through the rock to the lighthouse.

locationThemes.name: The Tide Well
locationThemes.purpose: A chamber with a deep well that rises and falls with the tide; here Halfdan sits in chains, guarded by the ghast that was Gorm Krogh.

locationThemes.name: The Lamp Room
locationThemes.purpose: The lamp room at the top of the Sortbro lighthouse, where the Wrecker’s Lantern burns green in place of the lighthouse lamp, and where Eske Sortfjer waits for the Three Sisters to run aground.

clueMap.conclusion: Halfdan is held prisoner in the caves beneath Sortbro, and the way there runs through the Sea Maw by Wreck Beach.

clues.observation: Every morning Halfdan’s left shoe stands on Vibeke’s doorstep, wet with seawater, with crushed shell sand in its seams and a faint smell of cinnamon, even though she took it indoors the evening before. It is a homing shoe, sewn by their mother. At night it seeks its owner for as long as he lives; if it cannot reach him, it walks home again before dawn.
clues.inference: Halfdan is somewhere by the sea where the sand is crushed shells, as on Wreck Beach below Sortbro, and he is alive: otherwise the shoe would not go out every night.

clues.observation: Halfdan’s logbook lies open on the table in the keeper’s room, its last pages written in an ever more hurried hand.
clues.inference: Halfdan saw lights and boats without lanterns in the Sea Maw and went down there on the night he vanished.
clues.handout:
3rd day of Harvestmonth: Lights in the Sea Maw again at low tide. Boats without lanterns.
4th day: E.S. asked for the key to the lamp room “for the council’s sake”. I said no.
5th day: Cinnamon on the wind from the cliff. Nobody bakes out here.
I am going down to the Sea Maw tonight to look.

clues.observation: At low tide a line of small, single shoeprints runs from the Sea Maw up towards the cliff path, with no trace of the other foot, and at the mouth of the cave there are drag marks of a man between two pairs of boots.
clues.inference: The shoe was inside the Sea Maw last night and walked home from there before dawn, and someone has dragged a man into the cave.

clues.observation: On a chest in the Cinnamon Cellar lies a note to the smuggler captain Ketil Vesterhavn, written in a fine merchant’s hand.
clues.inference: Halfdan is alive, held deeper in the caves and guarded by a ghast, and he is to be carried up to the lamp room at midnight. Of the town guard, whom Eske has promised the council to bring up to the lighthouse at that very hour, the note says nothing: the smugglers could be caught on the stair.
clues.handout:
Ketil.
The keeper is kept alive until midnight. The ghast guards him.
When the ship is broken, carry him up to the lamp room and go back down the stair.
No lanterns in the Sea Maw.
E.

clues.observation: High up in the east passage from the Sea Maw, above the high-water mark, small single shoeprints lead in towards the Tide Well and turn back ten paces short of the chamber, where the stench of rotten meat begins.
clues.inference: The shoe is seeking Halfdan in the Tide Well, but something there keeps it out.

clueMap.conclusion: Eske Sortfjer is behind the green light and Halfdan’s disappearance.

clues.observation: In the Anchor Inn the council’s old judgment hangs in a black frame above the fireplace, and that same evening Eske Sortfjer himself proposes that the town should have a new strand reeve.
clues.inference: The Sortfjer family has lured ships in before and lost the title for it; Eske has a motive to take it back.
clues.handout:
This day the Council of Ugletoft gives judgment:
The strand reeve of the Sortfjer line has been caught lighting false lights on Sortbro.
He and his line lose the title and the right to the wrecks for all time.
The title is given to the line of Bøgh.

clues.observation: A warm smell of cinnamon blows out of the Sea Maw, and nobody bakes out here; in Ugletoft only Eske Sortfjer deals in cinnamon.
clues.inference: The smell of cinnamon comes from the caves beneath Sortbro and leads to Eske’s spice trade.

clues.observation: In the logbook Halfdan has written that “E.S.” asked for the key to the lamp room “for the council’s sake”, and that Halfdan said no.
clues.inference: A councillor with the initials E.S. wanted to get into the lamp room; on the council only Eske Sortfjer has those initials.

clues.observation: The chests of cinnamon bark in the Cinnamon Cellar are branded with a black feather, the house mark of the Sortfjer family, and none of them bears the customs seal.
clues.inference: The smugglers work for Eske Sortfjer.

clueMap.conclusion: The ghast in the caves was once Councillor Gorm Krogh.

clues.observation: Thyra Bøgh tells them that Councillor Gorm Krogh disappeared a month ago and was declared drowned; Gorm always ate pickled onions from a jar in his coat pocket, and he had just asked in council why Eske’s goods never pay duty.
clues.inference: Gorm Krogh came too close to Eske’s business just before he disappeared.

clues.observation: Between the empty niches of the Chapel of the Drowned lie a broken jar of pickled onions and two links of a silver chain of office.
clues.inference: Gorm Krogh was here; it was not at sea that he died.

clues.observation: The ghast at the Tide Well wears the rags of a councillor’s coat, smells of vinegar and onions, and stops short when anyone says the name Gorm.
clues.inference: The monster is Gorm Krogh, transformed by the curse of the Wrecker’s Lantern, and a cleric may be able to reach the man he was.

partyMoments.moment: Pick the smugglers’ iron grate in the Sea Maw, find the hidden door behind the chapel altar, or get their old contact Ketil Vesterhavn talking before the fighting starts.
Reconsecrate the Chapel of the Drowned and give the drowned sailors peace, or call the ghast by the name Gorm Krogh and reach a last glimmer of the man.
Decipher the old inscription on the lantern’s brass frame and discover that only salt water from the Tide Well smothers the green fire.
Hold the narrow stair in the rock against the drowned while the others free Halfdan, or take on Ketil Vesterhavn in single combat on the slippery ledge in the Sea Maw.

scenes.title: The Shoe on the Doorstep
scenes.summary: At dusk in the Anchor Inn in Ugletoft the council quarrels over the green light above Sortbro, and Vibeke asks the heroes to find her brother. The heroes meet the suspects and get the first clues: the shoe, the old judgment against the Sortfjer family, and Thyra Bøgh’s words about Gorm Krogh.
scenes.readAloud: The Anchor Inn is thick with smoke and voices, and every window faces the cliff, where the lighthouse on Sortbro shines with a cold green glow. At the long table the councillors shout over one another, while a grey-haired woman sits silent at the head of the table with her hands folded. Beside your table stands a young woman holding a wet shoe, and a faint smell of cinnamon clings to her.
details: Vibeke shows them the shoe: Halfdan’s left shoe, wet with seawater, with crushed shell sand in its seams and a faint smell of cinnamon. It is a homing shoe that their mother sewed. At night it seeks its owner for as long as he lives; if it cannot reach him, it walks home again before dawn. Three evenings Vibeke has taken it indoors, and three mornings it has stood wet on her doorstep.
Above the fireplace hangs the council’s old judgment in a black frame; the councillors would rather not look at it.

Eske Sortfjer, councillor and the town’s spice merchant (the sign of the black feather hangs over his shop by the harbour, and all the cinnamon in Ugletoft is his), proposes that the town get a new strand reeve and promises the council to go up to the lighthouse with the town guard at midnight and “put an end to it”. He is friendly and concerned, and offers the heroes 100 gp to find “the mad keeper”.

Thyra Bøgh, the strand reeve, keeps silent until the heroes speak with her alone. Then she tells them that Councillor Gorm Krogh disappeared a month ago and was declared drowned; Gorm always ate pickled onions from a jar in his coat pocket, and he had just asked in council why Eske’s goods never pay duty.

Vibeke knows that Halfdan went out three nights ago and did not come home. His logbook is in the keeper’s room at the foot of the lighthouse, and the door up into the tower is barred from the inside. The lighthouse is half an hour away by the cliff path.
The council meeting lasts the first hour. Afterwards Eske goes home to his shop by the harbour and stays there until he leaves for Sortbro (see The Wrecker’s Lantern).

checks.success: Twice Eske speaks of “the family’s honour”, and he looks up at the green light with something like satisfaction; he has asked neither after Halfdan nor after the drowned sailors.
checks.failure: Eske seems a worried councillor; suspicion will have to come from the clues elsewhere.

checks.success: Thyra Bøgh gives the heroes the spare key to the keeper’s room and promises to hear them first when she comes up to the lighthouse with the guards at midnight.
checks.failure: Thyra does not trust strangers and tells them only about Gorm Krogh; the heroes get the key to the keeper’s room from Vibeke a quarter of an hour later.

checks.success: The heroes know the legend of the strand reeve who lit a green light on Sortbro, so that the drowned walked up the beach and carried his plunder ashore; in the legend only salt water could put the light out.
checks.failure: The heroes don’t know the legend; the innkeeper tells it for the price of an ale, but it takes a quarter of an hour.

alternatives: The heroes can follow Eske when he goes home after the meeting: the shop is locked, but in the yard behind it stands an empty chest marked with the black feather, and it smells strongly of cinnamon.
The rogue can ask around the harbour for their old contact Ketil Vesterhavn: he is not there, but a boy says that Ketil “sails cinnamon” at night.

When darkness falls, the shoe twists out of Vibeke’s hands and walks towards Sortbro. If the heroes follow it, it leads them down the cliff path to Wreck Beach and into the Sea Maw, then east towards the Tide Well.
scenes.dmNotes: Keep the meeting loud and quick: the council wants someone to blame, and Thyra Bøgh is the easy choice. Give the clues through people, not long explanations, and put the old judgment on the table as a handout. If the heroes linger, remind them of the grain ship’s lantern out in the fog.

scenes.title: The Keeper’s Room
scenes.summary: In the keeper’s room at the foot of the lighthouse on Sortbro the heroes find Halfdan’s logbook and the barred door up into the tower. The logbook and the smell of cinnamon from a crack in the cellar show them that the way to Halfdan and to the lamp room runs through the caves.
scenes.readAloud: The keeper’s room is low and cold, its fire long since dead. On the table a logbook lies open beside a cup with a skin of cold tea, and in the corner an oak door leads up into the tower. A faint smell of cinnamon rises through the floorboards, and high above the ceiling something hums in time with the green light.
details: Halfdan’s logbook lies open on the table, its last pages written in an ever more hurried hand.
In the logbook Halfdan has written that “E.S.” asked for the key to the lamp room “for the council’s sake”, and that he said no. Only one councillor has those initials: Eske Sortfjer.
Behind the logbook lies a drawing Halfdan made of a light he saw in the Sea Maw: a brass lantern with letters on its frame and a green flame.

The door up into the tower is barred with a crossbeam on the far side, and Halfdan’s bunch of keys is gone. It can be broken down (AC 15, 18 HP, or a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check), but the noise is heard in the lamp room, and the bodyguard stands ready at the top of the stair.
In the cellar beneath the room the smell of cinnamon seeps from a crack in the rock, and inside the crack faint footsteps sound: there is a stair inside the cliff.
From the keeper’s room a path runs a quarter of an hour down the cliff to Wreck Beach.

checks.success: The heroes see that the last lines were written at night with a new pen, and that Halfdan has drawn an arrow down towards the Sea Maw on the chart of the coast by the door.
checks.failure: The heroes spend another 20 minutes before they find the chart with the arrow.

checks.success: At the crack in the cellar the heroes hear voices inside the cliff: “At midnight we carry him up.” Now they know that a stair leads from the caves up into the tower.
checks.failure: The heroes notice only the draught and the smell of cinnamon from the crack.

alternatives: Break down the tower door and go straight to the lamp room; then Halfdan is still in the caves, and the bodyguard is warned.
Climb the outside of the tower to the gallery (see The Wrecker’s Lantern).
scenes.dmNotes: This is where the players put the pieces together. Give them the logbook as a handout and let them talk their own way to the Sea Maw. If they break the door down, let them: the fight in the lamp room simply comes sooner, and Halfdan is still missing.

scenes.title: The Caves beneath Sortbro
scenes.summary: From Wreck Beach the heroes enter the Sea Maw and go on to the Cinnamon Cellar, the Chapel of the Drowned and the Tide Well. They meet the smugglers, the drowned and the ghast that was Gorm Krogh, free Halfdan and find the stair up to the lamp room.
scenes.readAloud: From the beach a ledge of wet rock leads into the Sea Maw, where the surf booms beneath your feet. The light of your lanterns turns yellow and small, as if the darkness were drinking it. From the passages comes a smell of cinnamon, of seaweed, and of something sweet and rotten.
details: The way: from the lighthouse down to Wreck Beach, a quarter of an hour; through the caves from the Sea Maw to the Tide Well, half an hour without fights. After 4 hours the tide begins to fill the Sea Maw, and after 5 hours the way out to the beach is closed; then only the hidden stair behind the chapel altar leads out, up to the lamp room.
When the heroes first enter the Sea Maw, the lookout rings the bell and runs west to the chapel and up the stair (the clock’s second step), unless the heroes stop him.
The order is up to the players: the Cinnamon Cellar gives the key and the note, the chapel gives Gorm’s trail and the stair, the well gives Halfdan.
After 4 hours the drowned rise on Wreck Beach and walk in to the chapel; if the heroes meet them on the way, they walk past unless they are attacked.
Lanterns and torches go out after 1 minute in here (the Lantern’s Green Light; see the Lamp Room).

checks.success: The heroes reach the lookout on his rock shelf before he can ring; Eske is not warned and comes only after 4 hours.
checks.failure: The lookout rings and runs west; anyone who gives chase at once can catch him in the chapel before he reaches the stair.

checks.success: The heroes read the tide from the seaweed and know exactly when the Sea Maw will flood: after 5 hours.
checks.failure: The heroes notice the tide only when it is up to their knees in the Sea Maw.

checks.success: The heroes find the door behind the chapel altar without Halfdan’s help.
checks.failure: The heroes search for 10 minutes, or Halfdan shows them the door.

alternatives: Tell Ketil Vesterhavn that Eske is coming to the lighthouse with the town guard at midnight, so that the smugglers hand over the key and sail.
Bypass the Cinnamon Cellar by the passage from the Sea Maw straight to the Tide Well.
A cleric can reach Gorm Krogh with his name and the links of his chain of office.
scenes.dmNotes: Keep up the pace: each cave has its own choice between talking, sneaking and fighting. Keep an eye on the time; when the tide comes booming in, the players should feel the way back closing behind them. If the heroes free Halfdan early, let him tell them about the salt water and the stair, so they go up to the lamp room with a plan.

scenes.title: The Wrecker’s Lantern
scenes.summary: At the top of the lighthouse Eske Sortfjer stands by the Wrecker’s Lantern with his bodyguard and the lantern’s spirits, while the Three Sisters steers for the rocks. The heroes must put out the green fire, light the lighthouse’s true light and expose Eske before Thyra Bøgh and the town guard arrive at midnight.
scenes.readAloud: The last stair ends in a room of glass and green light. Behind the great lens a man in a fine dark cloak, a wet leather glove on one hand, stands looking out over the sea, where a ship’s lantern rocks slowly closer. Pale green shades of drowned sailors glide around the lens, and a broad figure with a sword steps out in front of the stair.
details: Eske Sortfjer is here after 4 hours, or an hour after the lookout has warned the lamp room, if that happened sooner. If the heroes arrive earlier, the bodyguard and the lantern’s spirits guard the lantern alone, and Eske comes up the stair from the chapel at that time, even in the middle of a fight.

The Three Sisters: from the lamp room the ship’s lantern can be seen drawing closer. If the green fire is not out and the lighthouse’s own lamp lit no later than 10 minutes before midnight, the ship is wrecked on Sortbro at midnight.
When the fight turns against him, Eske offers the heroes money and the right of wreck: “Half of everything the sea gives. What is one mad keeper against that?”

At midnight Thyra Bøgh and four of the town guard come up the tower stair from the keeper’s room. If they find Halfdan alive, the lantern out and the evidence (the note, the chests with the black feather, the logbook), they take Eske; if they find the heroes and Halfdan beside a burning lantern, they believe Eske.
Faced with the council’s old judgment, Halfdan alive and a witness from the council, Eske would rather confess than flee like a common wrecker.

checks.success: The heroes read the inscription on the lantern’s frame, “The sea gave the fire, the sea takes it back”, and know that salt water smothers the flame.
checks.failure: The inscription means nothing to them; Halfdan, or the legend from the Anchor Inn, can give them the answer.

checks.success: A hero climbs the outside of the tower to the gallery in 10 minutes and gets in through the panes behind the lens, past the bodyguard.
checks.failure: The hero slips, takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage while hanging on and needs another 10 minutes.

checks.success: With the evidence in front of him, Eske Sortfjer gives up, calls off his bodyguard and asks to be taken to the council, not through the crowd.
checks.failure: Eske denies everything and waits for the guards; now the evidence must speak for the heroes.

alternatives: Smother the lantern with a cloth dipped in the Tide Well, without fighting Eske.
Lure the bodyguard down the stair while someone else climbs up outside.
Let Eske talk: his pride in his family makes him say too much when Thyra Bøgh is standing in the doorway.
scenes.dmNotes: Let the clock tick loudly: the ship’s bell out in the fog, Eske’s calm voice, the spirits circling the lens. If the heroes put out the light while the ship is still on her way, give them the lighthouse’s true lamp as their last act. The ending depends on what Thyra Bøgh sees when she comes up.

locations.name: Wreck Beach
locations.readAloud: The beach below Sortbro is white with crushed mussel shells that crunch under every step. The wrecks of a cog and a fishing boat lie on the rocks, their ribs bared to the sky, and high above, the lighthouse burns with a cold green light. From the black opening in the cliff blows a warm breeze that smells of cinnamon.
locations.description: The path from the lighthouse runs a quarter of an hour down the cliff to the beach. At low tide one can walk dry-shod along the rocks into the Sea Maw; after 4 hours the tide begins to fill the cave, and after 5 hours the way in from here is closed. The drowned from the two wrecks stand out in the surf, under the water. After 4 hours they rise, walk up the beach and into the caves to the Chapel of the Drowned, where their fight is described; if the heroes meet them here, they walk past unless they are attacked.
features: A line of small, single shoeprints runs from the Sea Maw up towards the cliff path, with no trace of the other foot; at the mouth of the cave there are drag marks of a man between two pairs of boots. The shoeprints are from this morning, the drag marks three days old and half washed away by the tide. The tide has erased last night’s tracks into the cave.
A warm smell of cinnamon blows out of the Sea Maw. Nobody bakes out here, and in Ugletoft only Eske Sortfjer deals in cinnamon.
The cog’s hold has been emptied of everything of value, and someone has sawn off the ship’s nameboard. The fishing boat’s net hangs empty over the rail.
From the beach the lighthouse gallery can be seen 60 feet up; a climber can reach it by the stones of the tower.
treasure: In the cog’s forepeak lies the ship’s small strongbox, which the plunderers missed: 30 silver pieces and the skipper’s last letter to his wife, which Thyra Bøgh will gladly send on.

locations.name: The Sea Maw
locations.readAloud: The sea cave is as tall as a church, and the surf booms deep down in a hole in the middle of the floor. By the north wall an iron grate glints in the green glow that falls through a crack in the roof, and on a rock shelf hangs a small brass bell. Your lantern’s flame flutters, as if something were sucking the air out of it.
locations.description: The Sea Maw is the smugglers’ gate. In the middle of the floor a blowhole drops to the sea, and the surf spouts up through it with every wave. The north passage to the Cinnamon Cellar is barred by an iron grate, the east passage leads to the Tide Well and the west passage to the Chapel of the Drowned. The smugglers’ boat lies in a channel of water beneath the south wall. A lookout sits on the rock shelf by the bell: if he sees lights or hears strangers, he rings and runs west and up the hidden stair to warn the lamp room (the clock’s second step). The green light of the Wrecker’s Lantern (see the Lamp Room) reaches down here through the crack, so lanterns and torches go out after 1 minute. After 4 hours the tide begins to fill the cave; after 5 hours the water is chest-deep and the way out to the beach is closed.
features: The blowhole: with every wave the sea spouts 10 feet up out of the hole. Anyone standing at its edge must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or be knocked Prone.
The iron grate to the Cinnamon Cellar is locked: a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check with thieves’ tools opens it, or the key on the lookout’s belt.

The lookout is a young smuggler with no wish to fight. Caught or threatened, he tells them that Ketil and two men are waiting in the Cinnamon Cellar, that “the dead councillor” keeps watch at the well, and that nobody dares go in there without food for him.
The smugglers’ boat: two oars, a barrel of fresh water and three hooded lanterns.

High up in the east passage, above the high-water mark, small single shoeprints from last night lead in towards the Tide Well. Ten paces short of the chamber, where the stench of rotten meat begins, they turn back: the homing shoe could not get past the ghast.
locations.trap: An ankle-high tripwire just beyond the iron grate, tied to a bell in the Cinnamon Cellar. Anyone who looks for it finds it with a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check, and it is cut with a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. If anyone touches it, Ketil Vesterhavn and his crew are waiting behind the chests when the heroes arrive.

locations.name: The Cinnamon Cellar
locations.readAloud: The smell of cinnamon is so thick here that you can almost taste its sweetness. Chests and sacks stand stacked in tall rows, and above them looms an old figurehead of a woman with a fish’s tail, a lantern hung about her neck. Behind the chests men mutter, and a die rolls across a lid.
locations.description: The smugglers’ store. Ketil Vesterhavn and two of his crew wait here for midnight, dicing for their pay. Ketil does not fight for Eske but for his boat and his men: if the heroes tell him that Eske has promised the council to come up to the lighthouse with the town guard at midnight, he understands that his men could be caught on the stair with Halfdan and taken for the culprits (Eske’s note sends them up there at exactly that hour but mentions no guards), and with a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check, or for 50 gp, he hands over the key to Halfdan’s chain and sails as soon as the water allows. If the rogue knows him from before, the heroes have Advantage on the check. The south passage leads to the Sea Maw, the south-east passage to the Tide Well.
features: The chests of cinnamon bark are branded with a black feather, the house mark of the Sortfjer family, and none of them bears the customs seal.
On one chest lies a note to Ketil Vesterhavn, written in a fine merchant’s hand and signed “E.”
Ketil’s ledger: every week for a year, a cargo of cinnamon “for E.S.”, and on the last page “Councillor down into the chapel”, heavily underlined.
The figurehead comes from a ship the Sortfjer family plundered sixty years ago; the smugglers call her “Mistress Sortfjer” and hang their lantern around her neck for luck.
The key to Halfdan’s chain hangs on a cord around Ketil’s neck.

encounter.tactics: Ketil tries talking first: he wants to know who the heroes are and what they are offering. If it comes to a fight, the smugglers stay behind the chests and attack at range, while Ketil advances on the strongest hero. If Ketil or one of his men falls, the others beg for mercy; they fight for pay, not to die.
encounter.terrain: The stacks of chests give Half Cover. A stack can be toppled onto a foe with a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check: 2d6 Bludgeoning damage, and the foe is knocked Prone. The floor between the stacks is slippery with cinnamon dust.

treasure: Ketil’s pay in a canvas bag: 140 silver pieces and 30 gold pieces.
A chest of cinnamon bark with the black feather: worth 50 gp, but above all the best evidence against Eske Sortfjer for the council.

locations.name: The Chapel of the Drowned
locations.readAloud: A low grotto with niches cut into its walls, each holding an empty bier of driftwood and a withered wreath of seaweed. In one corner the roof has fallen in a heap of stones. The old altar is a block of black rock carved with a ship, and someone has smashed the offering bowls and scratched a feather into the stone.
locations.description: Here the town priest laid out the dead from the two wrecks before their burial. The light of the Wrecker’s Lantern raised them, and they walked out into the sea; the niches stand empty. Until 4 hours have passed, the chapel is empty. After 4 hours the drowned return here and guard the hidden stair behind the altar. Councillor Gorm Krogh was pushed down here a month ago and died at the Tide Well, where the curse turned him into a ghast. The east passage leads to the Sea Maw.
features: Between the empty niches lie a broken jar of pickled onions and two links of a silver chain of office.

The altar: someone has scratched a feather across the carved ship and smashed the offering bowls. A cleric who spends 10 minutes reconsecrating the altar (a DC 13 Intelligence (Religion) check, or no check with holy water) gives the chapel peace: as long as the Wrecker’s Lantern burns, the drowned do not enter the chapel but wait in the passage.
A cold draught and the smell of cinnamon come from the left side of the altar.
The heap of stones in the collapsed corner can be toppled into the east passage with a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check, blocking it against the drowned for 10 minutes.

encounter.tactics: Only after 4 hours. The drowned stand here guarding the stair behind the altar: the skipper keeps to the altar and shoots, while the sailors advance in a tight line. They do not pursue into the Sea Maw but return to the altar. If the Wrecker’s Lantern is put out, they collapse where they stand.
encounter.terrain: The biers in the niches give Half Cover, and the collapsed corner is Difficult Terrain. The stair behind the altar is so narrow that only one can fight there at a time.

treasure: The fishers’ offerings in a crack beneath the altar: 12 gold pieces in old coins and a small pewter fish, which a cleric would put back on the altar.
locations.secret: Behind the left side of the altar is a narrow stone door, painted to look like the rock. It is found with a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check, without a check by anyone who follows the draught and the smell of cinnamon, or because Halfdan shows it. Behind it a stair of 200 steps climbs through the rock to the lighthouse cellar and on up the tower to the lamp room: a quarter of an hour.

locations.name: The Tide Well
locations.readAloud: A round chamber where slick steps wind down into a black well, and the water in it breathes up and down with the sea. By the top step a man hangs in chains, his head sunk on his chest. On the rim of the well something hunched in rags sits gnawing, and a stench of rotten meat and vinegar fills the room.
locations.description: Halfdan sits chained to an iron ring by the well’s top step, weak (4 HP) but alive. Gorm Krogh, the ghast, guards him at the lantern’s bidding and attacks anyone who comes near Halfdan without the smugglers’ food. Two smugglers who drowned in the well on the first night stand down in the water and climb out when Gorm attacks. At high tide, after 5 hours, the water rises over the top three steps. The west passage leads to the Sea Maw, the north-west passage to the Cinnamon Cellar.
features: The ghast wears the rags of a councillor’s coat, smells of vinegar and onions, and stops short when anyone says the name Gorm.

Halfdan’s chain: AC 19, 10 HP, or its lock is picked with a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check using thieves’ tools; the key hangs around Ketil Vesterhavn’s neck. On a failure 10 minutes pass, and after the 4-hour mark the noise calls the drowned from the chapel.

If a cleric calls him Gorm Krogh and holds up the links of his chain of office, a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check makes Gorm step aside for 1 minute, mumbling in a thick voice: “Sortfjer … the lantern.”

Once Halfdan is free, he tells them: Eske Sortfjer was there himself on the first night, the lantern hangs in the lighthouse lens, the stair behind the chapel altar leads up there, and only salt water puts out the green fire (“Eske wet his glove in the sea before he touched it”).
The well’s water is seawater: a cloth dipped here smothers the flame of the Wrecker’s Lantern.

encounter.tactics: Gorm attacks the first person who moves towards Halfdan and tries to paralyse a hero and drag them down the steps. The drowned smugglers climb out of the well in the second round. If anyone says the name Gorm, he falters for a moment and loses his next Reaction. Gorm does not flee; if the Wrecker’s Lantern is put out, he collapses and is just a dead man in a councillor’s coat.
encounter.terrain: The steps down into the well are slick (see the Tide Well hazard), the chamber is only 50 feet across, and Halfdan’s chain is in the way by the top step.
encounter.hazard: The Tide Well. When: whenever a creature on the steps is hit or runs; after 5 hours the water covers the top three steps. Targets: creatures on the steps. Save: DC 10 Dexterity. Effect: the creature slides down into the well, takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage and is in the water; climbing out takes a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. Counter: a rope around the waist, or keeping to the chamber floor.

treasure: Halfdan’s right shoe, a homing shoe: together with the left one, which Vibeke has, it makes a pair. Whoever wears them always finds the way home. A shoe parted from its owner seeks him at night for as long as he lives; if it cannot reach him, it walks home again before dawn.

locations.name: The Lamp Room
locations.readAloud: At the top of the lighthouse the room is almost all glass: great panes all the way around, and in the middle the lighthouse lens, as tall as a man. In the heart of the lens hangs an old brass lantern, burning with a cold green flame that makes every other light grow pale. Outside, the fog rolls across the sea, and somewhere out in the dark a ship’s bell is ringing.
locations.description: The Wrecker’s Lantern hangs on the hook where the lighthouse’s own lamp used to hang; the lamp has been pushed under the bench. Until Eske Sortfjer arrives, his bodyguard, a former sellsword, guards the lantern together with three of the lantern’s spirits, specters of drowned sailors that hover around the lens. Eske comes after 4 hours, or an hour after the lookout has warned the lamp room (the clock’s second step), if that happens sooner. At midnight the Three Sisters is wrecked, unless the green fire is out and the lighthouse’s own lamp is lit. The stair from the chapel ends in the tower just below the lamp room; the door from the keeper’s room is barred with a crossbeam on this side.
features: The Wrecker’s Lantern: its brass frame bears an inscription in old letters (see the Lantern’s Green Light).

The lighthouse’s own lamp stands under the bench with a full oil reservoir. If it is lit in the lens again (1 minute), the lighthouse shows its true light, and the Three Sisters turns away from the rocks in time, provided at least 10 minutes remain until midnight.
From the gallery outside the panes the heroes can shout and wave lights at the ship, but only the lighthouse’s true light will turn her.
The gallery outside the panes hangs 60 feet above the rocks, with a rusty railing.

At midnight Thyra Bøgh and four of the town guard come up the tower stair, because Eske promised the council to put an end to the light. What they see when they arrive decides whom the council believes.

encounter.tactics: The bodyguard holds the top step of the stair, so the heroes can only come up one at a time. The lantern’s spirits glide through the lens and the panes and attack anyone who moves towards the lantern. Eske Sortfjer does not fight himself: he stays behind the lens, offers the heroes money and the right of wreck when the fight turns, and would rather surrender than die. If the lantern goes out, the spirits vanish, and the bodyguard gives up if Eske does.
encounter.terrain: The lamp room is only 20 feet across; the lens fills the middle and gives Half Cover. The panes can be smashed out onto the gallery, and the wind howls in.
encounter.hazard: The Lantern’s Green Light. When: all the time, as long as the lantern burns. Targets: every nonmagical flame in Ugletoft, on the cliffs and in the caves beneath Sortbro, and every drowned corpse within the light’s glow. Save: none. Effect: lanterns, torches and candles go out after 1 minute and must be lit again (an action); the drowned rise and obey whoever carries the lantern; ships at sea see a lighthouse that promises safe harbour. Counter: smash the lantern (AC 13, 6 HP), or smother the flame with a cloth soaked in salt water (an action within 5 feet); then the green fire goes out, the drowned collapse, the lantern’s spirits vanish and every light burns again. The inscription on the frame (a DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana) check) reads: “The sea gave the fire, the sea takes it back.”

treasure: Eske’s signet ring with the black feather.
The Wrecker’s Lantern, put out: an old brass lantern of no value, but the weightiest evidence against the Sortfjer family.

npcs.name: Eske Sortfjer
npcs.role: The villain: spice merchant and councillor of Ugletoft
npcs.look: A fine dark cloak with a feather of blackened silver on the breast, and a leather glove on his right hand that he never takes off.
npcs.personality: Courteous, patient and proud of a family nobody else is proud of.
npcs.wants: To be elected strand reeve at dawn and give the Sortfjer family back its honour.
npcs.secret: He carries his grandfather’s Wrecker’s Lantern and had the smugglers push Councillor Gorm Krogh down into the chapel. He wets his glove in salt water before he touches the lantern, for otherwise its cold flame burns into the flesh.
npcs.voice: Speaks low and slowly, as if reading out a judgment, and says “the family’s honour” more often than he realises.
npcs.where: At the Anchor Inn at dusk (The Shoe on the Doorstep); after 4 hours in the lamp room (The Wrecker’s Lantern).

npcs.name: Halfdan
npcs.role: The missing keeper of the Sortbro lighthouse
npcs.look: A big, bearded man wearing only one shoe, with a bruise around his wrist from the chain.
npcs.wants: To get the lighthouse’s true light burning again before more ships are lost.
npcs.secret: For years he ignored the smugglers’ lights in the Sea Maw in return for a barrel of cinnamon a year; only when the light in the lighthouse turned green did he say no.
npcs.voice: Answers in as few words as possible and counts the strokes of the ship’s bell aloud.
npcs.where: Chained at the Tide Well in the caves beneath Sortbro.

npcs.name: Vibeke
npcs.look: Wet sleeves, and the shoe held to her chest as if it were a child.
npcs.personality: Frightened, but not to be stopped.
npcs.wants: To bring her brother home before the council declares him guilty.
npcs.secret: She owes Eske Sortfjer money for her husband’s funeral and dares not say a bad word about him where the council can hear.
npcs.voice: Talks fast and holds out the shoe whenever anyone doubts her.
npcs.where: At the Anchor Inn at dusk, afterwards in her house by the harbour in Ugletoft.

npcs.name: Thyra Bøgh
npcs.role: Strand reeve of Ugletoft and eldest on the council
npcs.look: Grey hair in a tight braid, and the strand reeve’s brass horn on a twisted cord around her neck.
npcs.personality: Dry, fair-minded and tired of being suspected.
npcs.wants: To clear her name and keep the title her family has held for sixty years.
npcs.secret: She has long known that someone is smuggling cinnamon past the customs, but let it lie because she could not prove it against a councillor.
npcs.voice: Lets a pause hang before she answers, and taps two fingers on the table when she is sure.
npcs.where: At the council meeting in the Anchor Inn; at midnight in the lamp room with the town guard.

npcs.name: Gorm Krogh
npcs.role: The councillor who became a ghast
npcs.look: The rags of a councillor’s coat, a jar of pickled onions in the pocket, and a neck from which the chain of office has been torn.
npcs.personality: Hungry and confused, with a glimmer of a diligent, curious man.
npcs.wants: To eat, and, deep down, to be called by his name.
npcs.secret: Before he died he managed to scratch Eske’s feather into the mortar by the well; the tide has almost worn it away.
npcs.voice: Gnaws and mumbles, and says “Sortfjer … the lantern” when he hears his name.
npcs.where: At the Tide Well in the caves beneath Sortbro.

npcs.name: Ketil Vesterhavn
npcs.role: Smuggler captain in Eske’s pay and the rogue’s old contact
npcs.look: A gold tooth, a knife in his boot and cinnamon dust in his beard.
npcs.personality: Practical, greedy and loyal to his own.
npcs.wants: To get his pay and get away before anyone hangs.
npcs.secret: He suspects that Eske means to leave the smugglers holding the blame, and he has hidden a dinghy for himself at Wreck Beach.
npcs.voice: Calls everyone “mate” and weighs every coin in his hand before he answers.
npcs.where: In the Cinnamon Cellar in the caves beneath Sortbro.

rewards.name: Ketil’s Pay
rewards.description: A canvas bag holding 140 silver pieces and 30 gold pieces, the smugglers’ payment for a year of cinnamon.

rewards.name: The Cog’s Strongbox
rewards.description: A small chest holding 30 silver pieces and the skipper’s last letter to his wife, which Thyra Bøgh will gladly send on.

rewards.name: The Fishers’ Offerings
rewards.description: Old coins and a small pewter fish in a crack beneath the altar. A cleric who puts them back earns the fishers’ gratitude and a free passage, any time.

rewards.name: The Council’s Thanks
rewards.where: At the council meeting at dawn, once Eske is exposed
rewards.description: Thyra Bøgh pays from the strand reeve’s coffers and says so aloud, so that the whole Anchor Inn hears it.

rewards.name: Eske’s Signet Ring
rewards.description: A silver ring bearing the black feather of the Sortfjer family; the council wants it as evidence but repays its value.

rewards.name: The Homing Shoes
rewards.where: Halfdan’s right shoe at the Tide Well, and the left one from Vibeke as thanks
rewards.description: A pair of worn keeper’s shoes, sewn by Halfdan’s mother. Whoever wears them has Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to find the way back to the place where they last slept safely. A shoe parted from its owner seeks them at night for as long as they live; if it cannot reach them, it walks home again before dawn.

rewards.name: The Skipper’s Compass
rewards.where: The cog’s skipper in the Chapel of the Drowned
rewards.description: A brass compass from the cog whose needle points to the nearest drowned body within a mile. A cleric who uses it has Advantage on checks to find the dead who need to be laid to rest.

endings.success: Thyra Bøgh and the town guard find Halfdan alive, the Wrecker’s Lantern out and the lighthouse’s true light burning, while the Three Sisters glides safely past Sortbro. Faced with his note, the chests with the black feather and the logbook, Eske Sortfjer is led away and confesses, and the Wrecker’s Lantern is thrown into the sea from Sortbro. At dawn the council gives Thyra back her title with thanks, Gorm Krogh is buried in consecrated ground with his chain of office, and Halfdan and Vibeke give the heroes the homing shoes.
endings.partial: The green light is put out, but too late to turn the Three Sisters fully: the ship tears her hull open on the outermost skerry and reaches the harbour half full of water, and some sailors drown. Or Halfdan is saved, but Eske escapes down the stair and out to sea with the smugglers at the next low tide. The council clears Thyra Bøgh and Halfdan, but Eske is a wanted man, still has friends on the council and knows who the heroes are.
endings.failure: At midnight the Three Sisters is wrecked on Sortbro, and twenty sailors drown and walk up the beach as Eske’s new drowned. Eske ‘finds’ Halfdan beside the lantern in front of the town guard, and at dawn Thyra Bøgh is stripped of her title, Halfdan is hanged as the mad keeper and Eske Sortfjer is elected strand reeve. The next ship to approach Ugletoft sees a green light on Sortbro, and the heroes are the ones the council now suspects.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes accuse Eske Sortfjer openly in the Anchor Inn without evidence.
unexpected.response: The council laughs and calls them Thyra Bøgh’s hired hands; Eske stays courteous but goes to Sortbro after only 2 hours, to be safe. The clues are still where they were.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes break down the tower door and storm the lamp room before they have found Halfdan.
unexpected.response: The fight in the lamp room happens now. If they put out the lantern, the drowned fall, but Halfdan is still chained at the well; Eske, or the bodyguard, says the smugglers will drown the keeper if the heroes don’t leave. Ketil would not do it, but the heroes don’t know that.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes kill Gorm Krogh without knowing who he was.
unexpected.response: As he falls, the jar of pickled onions rolls out of his coat, and Halfdan says: “That was Councillor Krogh.” The council still gets its witness, and the cleric can still give him peace.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes want to take the Wrecker’s Lantern with them instead of putting it out.
unexpected.response: The lantern obeys whoever carries it: the drowned now follow the heroes, and every lantern in Ugletoft still goes out after a minute. Thyra Bøgh wants to see it put out, and whoever keeps it earns a wrecker’s name.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes row out in the smugglers’ boat to warn the Three Sisters directly.
unexpected.response: In the fog and the surf it takes a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check to reach the ship in time. The crew trust a lighthouse more than shouts from a boat, but a lantern swung from the boat makes the mate heave to for 10 minutes; the green fire must still be put out.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes bring Thyra Bøgh and the town guard along from the start.
unexpected.response: Thyra comes gladly, but the guards flee when they see the drowned, and Eske keeps away from the lighthouse until he hears that the heroes are down in the caves. Thyra is a witness, but the heroes must still find the evidence themselves.

tips: Put the shoe, the council’s old judgment and the logbook on the table as handouts; the mystery is carried by things the players can hold in their hands.
Keep the clock visible: note down the grain ship’s lantern and the tide, and let every hour be felt in the caves with lanterns going out, surf and bells.
Let Eske be likeable in the first scene; it makes the reveal better.
Gorm Krogh is the cleric’s moment: give the player time to say the name.
If the fight in the lamp room gets too hard, remind the players that the lantern is the key, not the spirits: a wet cloth, a well-aimed throw or the lighthouse’s own lamp.
sequelHooks: The strand reeve of the Sortfjer line had more than one lantern: in the family crypt hangs one more empty hook, and a green light has been seen at a lighthouse further down the coast.
The grain ship’s skipper owes the heroes his ship and asks them to escort his next cargo through waters where Ketil Vesterhavn’s old crew lies in wait for revenge.

history.note: English edition of TT-C1, translated from Danish by Claude Opus 5.5
